claims.text: Different countries have their own currencies.
claims.quote: Different countries have their own currencies.

claims.text: An exchange rate is written as one unit of a foreign currency equal to an amount in rands, for example euro 1 = R10,68, pound 1 = R12,41 and 1 kr = R1,37.
claims.quote: if the exchange rate is currently \euro{} $\text{1}$ $=$ $\text{R10,68}$

claims.text: To find the cost in rands of an amount priced in a foreign currency, use the exchange rate in rands per unit of the foreign currency: with pound 1 = R12,41 a price of pound 4 is R49,64, and with 1 kr = R1,37 a price of 48 kr is R65,76 (the foreign amount multiplied by the rate).
claims.quote: this means that a Big Mac in England costs $\text{R49,64}$ and a Big Mac in Norway costs $\text{R65,76}$

claims.text: To find how much foreign currency a rand amount buys, write down the equation by letting the equivalent amount in the foreign currency (euros) be x.
claims.quote: Let the equivalent amount in euros be $x$

claims.text: To buy foreign currency with rands, divide the amount of rands by the exchange rate (rands per unit of the foreign currency): x = 10 000 / 10,68 = 936,33 euros.
Write the final answer as a sentence stating the amount of foreign currency bought with the rands: Saba can buy euro 936,33 with R10000.
The three currencies most likely to be seen are the British pound (pound sign), the American dollar ($) and the euro (euro sign).
claims.quote: The three currencies you are most likely to see are the British pound (£), the American dollar ( $\$$ ) and the euro (\euro).

claims.text: A currency gets stronger when money is invested in the country.
claims.quote: A currency gets stronger when money is invested in the country.

items.stem: Saba wants to travel to see her family in Spain. She has been given $\text{R10000}$ spending money. How many euros can she buy if the exchange rate is currently \euro{} $\text{1}$ $=$ $\text{R10,68}$ ?
solution: Write down the equation: Let the equivalent amount in euros be $x$ $\begin{align*}x&=\frac{\text{10 000}}{\text{10,68}}\\&=\text{936,33}\end{align*}$
Write the final answer: Saba can buy \euro{} $\text{936,33}$ with $\text{R10000}$ .

items.stem: Bridget wants to buy an iPod that costs $\text{£ 100}$ , with the exchange rate currently at $\text{£ 1}$ $=$ $\text{R14}$ . She estimates that the exchange rate will drop to $\text{R12}$ in a month. How much will the iPod cost in rands, if she buys it now?
solution: Cost in rands = (cost in pounds) $\times$ exchange rate. $=100\times\frac{14}{1}=\text{R1400}$

items.stem: Study the following exchange rate table: CountryCurrencyExchange RateUnited Kingdom (UK)Pounds (£) $\text{R14,13}$ United States (USA)Dollars ( $\$$ ) $\text{R7,04}$ In South Africa the cost of a new Honda Civic is $\text{R173400}$ . In England the same vehicle costs $\text{£12 200}$ and in the USA $\$ \text{21\ 900}$ . In which country is the car the cheapest?
solution: To answer this question we work out the cost of the car in rand for each country and then compare the three answers to see which is the cheapest. Cost in rands = cost in currency times exchange rate. Cost in UK: $\text{12 200}\times\frac{\text{14,13}}{\text{1}}=\text{R172 386}$ Cost in USA: $\text{21\900}\times\frac{\text{7,04}}{1}=\text{R154400}$ Comparing the three costs we find that the car is the cheapest in the USA.
items.epub_final_answer: Comparing the three costs we find that the car is the cheapest in the USA.

Sollie gets a $\text{£ 6}$ tip from a tourist and Arinda gets $\$\text{12}$ . Who got the better tip?

items.stem: Yaseen wants to buy a book online. He finds a publisher in London selling the book for $\text{£7,19}$ . This publisher is offering free shipping on the product. He then finds the same book from a publisher in New York for $\text{\$ 8,49}$ with a shipping fee of $\$\text{2}$ . Next he looks up the exchange rates to see which publisher has the better deal. If $\text{\$1}=\text{R11,48}$ and $\text{£1}=\text{R17,36}$ , which publisher should he buy the book from?
solution: London publisher: $\text{7,19}\times\frac{\text{17,36}}{1}=\text{R124,82}$ New York publisher: $(\text{8,49}+2)\times\frac{\text{11,48}}{1}=\text{R120,43}$ . Therefore Yaseen should buy the book from the New York publisher.
items.epub_final_answer: Therefore Yaseen should buy the book from the New York publisher.

pairs.reason: Both say buy from the New York publisher.

items.stem: Mathe is saving up to go visit her friend in Germany. She estimates the total cost of her trip to be $\text{R50000}$ . The exchange rate is currently $\text{€ 1}=\text{R 13,22}$ . Her friend decides to help Mathe out by giving her $\text{€1000}$ . How much (in rand) does Mathe now need to save up?
solution: We first calculate how much Mathe's friend will give her in rands: $\text{1000}\times\frac{\text{13,22}}{\text{1}}=\text{R13220}$ . Therefore Mathe now needs to save up: $\text{R50 000}-\text{R13 220}=\text{R36 780}$ .

items.stem: Kayla is planning a trip to visit her family in Malawi followed by spending some time in Tanzania at the Serengeti. She will first need to convert her South African rands into the Malawian kwacha. After that she will convert her remaining Malawian kwacha into Tanzanian shilling. She looks up the current exchange rates and finds the following information: $\begin{align*}\text{R1}&=\text{39,46MWK}\\\text{1MWK}&=\text{4,01TZS}\end{align*}$ She starts off with $\text{R5000}$ in South Africa. In Malawi she spends $\text{65 000 MWK}$ . When she converts the remaining Malawian kwacha to Tanzanian shilling, how much money does she have (in Tanzanian shilling)?
solution: We first convert from rands to Malawian kwacha: $\text{5000}\times\frac{\text{39,46}}{\text{1}}=\text{197 300MWK}$ She spends $\text{65 000 MWK}$ of this and so she has $\text{132 300 MWK}$ to convert to Tanzanian shillings. Now we can convert from Malawian kwacha to Tanzanian shillings: $\text{132 300MWK}\times\frac{\text{4,01}}{\text{1}}=\text{530 523TZS}$ So she will have $\text{530 523 TZS}$ to spend in Tanzania.
items.epub_final_answer: So she will have 530 523 TZS to spend in Tanzania.

items.stem: Bonani won a trip to see Machu Picchu in Peru followed by a trip to Brazil for the carnival. He is given $\text{R25000}$ to spend while on the trip. He then looks up the current exchange rates and finds the following information: $\begin{align*}\text{R1}&=\text{0,26PEN}\\\text{1BRL}&=\text{1,17PEN}\end{align*}$ In Peru he spends $\text{2380PEN}$ . When he converts the remaining Peruvian sol to Brazilian real, how much money does he have (in Brazilian real)?
solution: We first convert from rand to Peruvian sol: $\text{25 000}\times\frac{\text{0,26}}{\text{1}}=\text{6500PEN}$ He spends $\text{2380PEN}$ of this and so he has $\text{4120PEN}$ to convert to Brazilian real. Now we can convert from Peruvian sol to Brazilian real: $\text{4120PEN}\times\frac{\text{1}}{\text{1,17}}=\text{3521,37BRL}$ So he will have $\text{3521,37 BRL}$ to spend in Brazil.
items.epub_final_answer: So he will have 3521,37 BRL to spend in Brazil.
